1.explanation:
• cli/cli-flags.js: This file maps the `--screenEmulation.disabled` and `--no-emulatedUserAgent` CLI flags into the internal `configSettings`. If those flags aren’t turning off device emulation in the config as expected, we’ll still pick up the default mobile form factor and device name downstream.

• core/lib/emulation.js: Contains the logic that, given a form factor and screen emulation settings, picks a device definition (such as Moto G4) and applies viewport & userAgent overrides. Because screenEmulation is disabled, this module should detect a real‐device run and _not_ pick a built-in emulation profile, but it currently does.

• core/config/default-config.js: Defines the default `formFactor` and `screenEmulation` settings (defaulting to mobile/Moto G4). Even though the CLI flags should override these defaults, any mis-merge here will leave the defaults in place and trigger emulation downstream.

• report/renderer/report-ui-features.js: Builds the list of “features” that get shown in the report footer (form factor/device, throttling, UA, etc.). It currently sees `formFactor: 'mobile'` and a non-empty emulated device profile and emits an “Emulated Moto G4” entry.

• report/renderer/topbar-features.js: Renders the actual DOM for each feature entry in the footer, including the device icon and the “Emulated ${deviceName}” text. This is where the default emulation label is surfaced; it will need logic to swap in “Real device” when emulation is truly disabled.

Together, these files coordinate how flags become configSettings, how emulation profiles are selected, and how the report footer describes the run environment. Fixing the bug will require changes in the CLI flag handling (to truly disable any emulation profile), in the emulation logic (to detect a physical device session and clear out the device name), and in the report UI (to render a “real device” label instead of “emulated”).
1.bug_scenario: When Lighthouse is run from the CLI against a physical Android device (in the example, a Moto Power G) with both screen‐emulation and UA‐spoofing explicitly disabled, the generated HTML report footer still says “Emulated Moto G4 with Lighthouse 9.6.8” (and shows the Moto G4 icon), rather than acknowledging that it was run on a real device.

2.explanation:
• cli/cli-flags.js defines and parses both the --screenEmulation.disabled and --no-emulatedUserAgent flags, but downstream code never uses those flags to suppress the “Emulated” device badge.  
• core/config/config-helpers.js is where Lighthouse merges your CLI flags into its default mobile configuration, yet it doesn’t clear out the `emulatedFormFactor` or `screenEmulation` device settings when you disable emulation.  
• core/runner.js takes the merged config and produces the final `settings` object (including `formFactor` and `emulatedFormFactor`), but even with emulation disabled it still leaves the mobile form factor and default device name in place.  
• core/lib/emulation.js holds the mapping between viewport metrics and the known device names (e.g. Moto G4). It is consulted when building the default device label—even on a real device whose dimensions match the Moto G4, so the report always resolves back to that emulated name.  
• report/renderer/topbar-features.js is responsible for rendering the top-bar badges (“Emulated Moto G4…”, “Slow 4G throttling”, etc.). It uses the `settings.emulatedFormFactor` and device name unconditionally, so it never offers a “Real device” badge alternative.  

To fix this bug you would:  
1. In config-helpers / runner, respect the --screenEmulation.disabled and --no-emulatedUserAgent flags by clearing out or changing the `emulatedFormFactor` and device name when running on a real device.  
2. Adjust core/lib/emulation.js to skip the viewport-to-device lookup if emulation is disabled.  
3. Update report/renderer/topbar-features.js to render a “Testing on a real device” badge instead of the “Emulated …” badge when those flags are set or when a physical port is in use.
2.bug_scenario: When running Lighthouse CLI against a real Android device (a Moto Power G) with screen emulation disabled, no UA spoofing, and DevTools-based throttling, the generated HTML report still labels the run as “Emulated Moto G4 with Lighthouse 9.6.8” and shows the Moto G4 icon. In other words, despite hitting a physical device, Lighthouse’s footer badge stays locked to its default “Emulated” device name.
